notes: Demand-side composition and incidence parameters. Every rate below is an observed anchor already carried in `14` §2 with its evidence note; the derived rates, the denominator-sensitivity factor, the augmentation elasticity and the incidence identity are D-grade report-side calculations. No new numeric identity is created and no propensity is asserted — the one ratio the evidence does not pin down stays a dial.

adoption_panel_btos.base: U.S. firms; AI use in at least one business function; same instrument, same denominator
adoption_panel_btos.source_identity: Census BTOS, via 14 §2 evidence note B

adoption_panel_cross_country.source_identity: cross-country survey via 14 §2 evidence note C
adoption_panel_cross_country.combination_rule: Kept separate from the BTOS panel. It is used only as a denominator-sensitivity demonstration, never pooled or averaged with it, because the population, the question and the recall window all differ.

incidence.identity: demand_effect = employment_effect x rho, where rho = consumption propensity of the displaced / average consumption propensity
incidence.note: rho is deliberately a dial. 14 §3 gate G2 states that the claim that high income deciles drive a disproportionate share of spending is a scenario assumption until stated with its own same-denominator source; the repository carries no propensity-by-cohort panel. The identity is the result, and it is what bounds the demand leg — not the dial.
